name: Yang Yuanqing
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026)
forbes_bio: Yang Yuanqing is chairman and CEO of Lenovo, one of China's largest makers of computer hardware.
He joined the company in 1989 and became its CEO twenty years later.
An engaging leader, Yang speaks frequently at conferences (lately on A.I.) and posts often about his business activities on social media.
He sits on the board of Chinese search giant Baidu as an independent director, a post he's held since 2015.

name: Lillyn Teh Li Hua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Lillian Teh Li Hua is the daughter of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who chaired the Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank for several decades.
Teh Hong Piow founded the bank in 1966. He died in December 2022 at age 92.
In addition to Malaysia, the bank serves millions of customers across Cambodia, China, Hong Kong, Sri Lanka and Vietnam.
Teh had a significant minority stake in the bank as well as in the listed insurance business, LPI Capital.

name: Madhusudan Agarwal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2021-2024)
forbes_bio: Madhusudan Agarwal, who was running Delhi-based Haldiram Foods, merged his company with his cousin's Nagpur-based Haldiram Foods International in 2023 to create Haldiram Snacks Food.
A consortium of investors led by Singapore's Temasek, acquired a 20% stake in the merged company in 2025 at an estimated valuation of $10 billion.
Agarwal is the grandson of founder Ganga Bishan Agarwal, who started selling snacks from a tiny shop in Bikaner in Rajasthan in 1937 and went on to create the popular Haldiram brand.
The business was eventually divided among the patriarch's grandsons into three separate companies, operating out of Nagpur, Delhi and Kolkata.

name: Anita Zucker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Anita Zucker is chair and CEO of Charleston, South Carolina-based InterTech Group, a private, family-owned chemicals manufacturer.
InterTech was founded in 1982 by Zucker's late husband, Jerry, who died of a brain tumor in 2008 at age 58.
The company, which has estimated revenues of roughly $3 billion, also owns an aerospace engineering firm and extensive commercial real estate.
Jerry Zucker, an immigrant from Israel, was a prolific inventor who was granted numerous patents.
forbes_facts: The daughter of a holocaust survivor, Zucker is a former elementary school teacher.

name: Shyam Bhartia
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2021)
forbes_bio: Shyam Bhartia chairs the Jubilant Bhartia group with interests in energy, fast food, pharma and auto distribution.
The Jubilant group has four listed companies.
Jubilant Foodworks has hundreds of Domino's Pizza outlets across India.
Jubilant Life Sciences was split into two companies, Jubilant Pharmova and Jubilant Ingrevia. The latter was listed in March 2021.
His younger brother Hari, who is also a billionaire, is co-chairman.
forbes_facts: Bhartia's wife Shobhana has her separate media company, which publishes the Hindustan Times daily newspaper.
In February 2025, a police case was filed against him for allleged rape and criminal intiimdation of an aspiring Bollywood actress. Bhartia denied the allegations.
In December 2024, the Bhartia brothers acquired a 40% stake in Coca Cola's Indian bottler for 125 billion rupees ($1.5 billion).

name: Pacal Vanhalst
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025)
forbes_bio: Pascal Vanhalst's fortune stems from Thermote & Vanhalst, also known as TVH Parts, a supplier of spare parts for industrial and agricultural equipment.
He inherited part of the company from his father, Paul Vanhalst, who started TVH with his friend Paul Thermote to repair and resell forklift trucks.
He's reinvested a significant part of his wealth by acquiring European companies through his investment vehicle Quva Invest.

name: Ge Tairong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2025-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Ge Tairong derives his wealth from a stake in Zhengjiang Rongtai Electric Material, a producer of temperature-resistant mica tapes.
His wife, Cao Meisheng, is the company's chairman and CTO.
Zhejiang Rongtai supplies to sectors including robotics and new energy vehicles.
It went public in Shanghai in 2023, raising $151 million.

name: Mark Kurtser
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Mark Kurtser is the founder and majority shareholder of MD Medical Group, one of Russia's largest healthcare providers, with 90 locations operating under the brand "Mat I Ditya" (Mother and Child).

Kurtser is a physician who formerly served as head of the Centre for Family Planning and Reproduction, Moscow's largest state maternity hospital. At the same time, he was the Chief Obstetrician-gynecologist of the Moscow Healthcare Department.

A former educator with the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of the Pirogov Russian National Research Medical University, he founded MD in 2006, which later opened the first private maternity hospital in Moscow.
MD Medical was listed in London in 2012 and now trades on the Moscow Stock Exchange.
Kurtser, who sold shares worth $140 million in the IPO, invested in a number of Russian healthcare startups.

name: Shin Dong-joo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2016)
forbes_bio: Shin Dong-joo is the eldest son of Shin Kyuk-Ho, the late founder of Lotte Group, one of South Korea's largest conglomerates.
The retail heavyweight has interests ranging from food and beverage to chemicals, construction and professional baseball.
In 2015, he was dismissed from his executive positions in the group after a bitter feud with his brother Dong-Bin.
forbes_facts: Lotte started as a confectionery manufacturer in Japan in 1948 and expanded into South Korea in 1967.
At the start of his career, he worked for Mitsubishi in Japan in 1978.

name: Xiong Wu

The Shenzhen-headquartered company has more than 9,500 employees.
